incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Elevated 5xx + timeouts observed from private-vpc inference-gateway (us-west-2). Error rate >3% over 5m, customers affected. Auto-escalating to oncall.
Sam: I'm on it — taking pager. any obvious recent deploys to the private stack?
Mike (support): getting a few DMs from customers reporting 504s and slow responses since ~10:10 PT. top complaint: model calls time out, retries spike.
Anya: no infra deploys. I just checked deployment logs, nothing changed in control-plane for private-vpc.
Sam: ok start with quick health checks: can someone pull gateway logs and NAT metrics? curious about conntrack and SNAT exhaustion.
Lee: pulling CloudWatch for nat-ephemeral-usage now. seeing a spike in ActiveConnections and a 5xx tail in gateway logs around 10:08.
Sam: paste logs here (trimmed):
```
2024-03-28T17:08:12Z inference-gw[az-a]: upstream=10.0.5.12:443 status=504 path=/v1/generate
2024-03-28T17:08:15Z nat-gw[usw2-az1]: conntrack_alloc_failed
2024-03-28T17:08:19Z inference-gw[az-a]: upstream=10.0.7.33:443 status=502 path=/v1/chat
```
Anya: conntrack_alloc_failed lines match a nat/conntrack exhaustion. also seeing ephemeral port churn in nat metrics.
infra-bot: NAT ephemeral ports used: 94% (threshold 85%). Alert triggered.
Sam: ok likely root cause = ephemeral SNAT port exhaustion on private NAT gateway -> backend connections failing -> 502/504. Is this only one AZ?
Lee: traffic concentration in az-a, az-b fine. peering load shifted because a transit appliance failed earlier, we rerouted. that hub reroute pushed more flows from many hosts -> ephemeral hotspot.
Mike (support): list of affected customers: cust-a, cust-b, cust-c. cust-a is hitting production fallback and seeing degraded UX.
Sam: mitigation plan: 1) reduce fanout from clients -> apply temporary egress SG to limit burst? 2) add additional NAT / scale out / rotate to spare NATs, 3) short-term failover routes for priority customers to hosted inference path.
Anya: SG tweak could be risky (may block legitimate traffic). prefer scale out NAT or add an EIP-backed NAT in the same AZ. I'm spinning up an extra NAT instance now.
Ops (oncall): do we need a config change in route table or just add NAT target behind existing gateway? might need test before switching.
Sam: we can add a second NAT and update the autoscaling group for NATs. while that happens, let's throttle connection reuse from our proxies: reduce simultaneous upstream TCP connections via nginx limit_conn.
Lee: injecting nginx config change on inference-gw in az-a (hotfix):
```
limit_conn_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=addr:10m;
limit_conn addr 40;
```
Sam: pushing now — will monitor error rates.
infra-bot: NAT new instance spun up: nat-standby-03 in az-a (initializing).
Mike (support): informed cust-a + cust-b that we're investigating and implementing mitigations. added ETA ~15m for visible improvement.
Sam: prometheus graphs — error rate down from 3.4% -> 1.2% within 3m of nginx limits but still some 502s as nat-standby warms.
Anya: NAT instance ready. updating route targets to include nat-standby-03 for private-subnet-1.
Sam: routes updated, conntrack now shows allocations stabilizing. ephemeral usage dropping to 62%.
Lee: post-change logs look healthier, only occasional 502s for old flows. new connections succeed.
Mike (support): customers reporting gradual recovery, cust-c still sees intermittent errors but much improved.
Sam: creating a short-lived escalation ticket for runbook followups: need long-term fixes: increase NAT capacity, add conntrack tuning, and change peering failover strategy to avoid sudden fanout to single AZ.
Anya: agreed. also recommend enabling prefix-gap for egress pooling and implement flow aggregation on proxies.
Ops (oncall): handoff to infra for overnight monitoring. I'll update incident channel and SRE rotation.
Sam: marking incident as mitigated for now. will keep watch for 60m then close. thanks team :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Incident note: mitigation applied (nginx conn limits, added NAT instance) — monitor window started.
Mike (support): I'll follow up with customers with a postmortem ETA.
Sam: quick postmortem action items: (1) scale NAT capacity (2) add conntrack alert earlier (3) review peering reroute automation. I'll open tickets.
Anya: copying infra runbook steps into ticket + rollback notes for nginx change.
Ops (oncall): handing off to night shift. if error rate >1% alert me immediately. :bell:
Sam: thanks, handing off. all participants please ack if you saw this.
Anya: ack
Mike (support): ack
Lee: ack
Ops (oncall): ack
